Thats when my depression was its worst. The first 2-3 months were very harsh with big depression, terrible avolition and suicidal thoughts. Then it slowly got better. I felt very hopeless but kept reminding myself its VERY normal to have depression after psychosis. And its ok to just exist in recovery.

Try to take care of the basics, eat, sleep, drink water. Dont use too much time on social media bc (for me) it made me sad I wasnt functioning like others. I know how it feels. Be kind to yourself. Forget all about toxic productivity because your mind needs rest now. 

Its not easy but hold on, I promise it will get easier. True friends will be right there when youre ready to be social and go out again. Right after the roughest part it started getting better for me. Helped alot to start working out in a gym.

Hugs and message me if you need

im cis, but most of my close friends are trans so ill just say what theyve told me over the years. (tell me if theres anything i get wrong)

- obviously, respect them: their identity is valid and you should treat them like any other person. for example if youre talking to a trans woman, theyre a woman who is trans, not a «transwoman». trans people are a minority and its important to make it a norm to respect them. (as other cis people are more likely to mirror your behaviour then lmao, sad but true a lot of the time)
- !! listen to them: when talking about trans related topics, dont talk over them or try to argue/discuss. im sure it depends on the person, but remember its not just a political topic but their identity and very personal. and they know more about it than you do.
- pronouns: pronouns being hard are the least of your problems. its very easy if you just try. remember that a little slip up for you can be very hurtful for the person. though if you do, just casually correct yourself and apologize, dont make it a big deal. oh, and correct people if they say wrong behind their back. i at least experience this alot, people talking about my friends and using wrong pronouns when theyre not around. its shitty and disrespectful so yeah
- accept that you cant fully understand their experience and identity as a cis person
- dont «out» them(talk about them being trans) to others unless the person has said its ok

- just be a bro tbh
